system.name: celld
system.description: A self-hosted daemon that runs a Cloudflare Workers application, with its Durable Objects, KV, Queues, D1, R2, Workflows, Cron Triggers, static assets, Dynamic Workers and containers, on the operator's own machines, keeping long-term state in the operator's object-storage bucket.

corpus.included: The whole denoland/celld repository at the revision below and its version-control history (14 release commits, v0.0.1 to v0.6.3): crates/celld, crates/logic, crates/ltx, docs, examples, README.md, the release workflow, the Dockerfile and the manifests.
corpus.excluded: Dependencies (Cargo.lock and the crates it names), generated output and secrets, none of which besides Cargo.lock is tracked. Test suites and design documents that the code includes or cites from outside the tree are not part of the repository.

consumers.name: Application developer
consumers.description: A person who writes a Cloudflare Workers project, with its Workers, Durable Objects and bindings in a wrangler.json, and runs it on celld without changing it.

consumers.name: Fleet operator
consumers.description: A person who runs celld nodes on their own machines against a bucket they own and keeps that fleet running as it grows, shrinks and upgrades; their orchestrator, autoscaler and load balancer act for them.

providers.name: celld
providers.description: The celld daemon and command line, with the bucket layout they share, as their users see them: one fleet of nodes that runs one Workers application.

parts.name: Operator command-line clients
parts.why: celld d1, kv and queue sign a request to a live node's /runtime/ route, which forwards it to the owner, and celld r2 and celld cell read and write the bucket through the node's own record modules; they present the node's capabilities, so they are part of the celld command line interface.

parts.name: Local development stack
parts.why: celld dev runs the deploy path and one supervised node against a SQLite stand-in for the object store, which both of them write; it is the local development server interface, not a component.

parts.name: Object store client
parts.why: bucket.rs is the single adapter every part uses to reach the bucket.

parts.name: Process facilities
parts.why: The execution facade, environment parsing, machine and memory sampling, listener startup and the outbound WebSocket client are libraries.

components.name: Deployment publisher
components.description: Turns a Wrangler project into a deployment: it checks the configuration against what celld supports, bundles the Worker with esbuild or packs a Python Worker with Pyodide, packs the static assets and container images, and writes them to the bucket as the records nodes read.

parts.name: Wrangler config translation
parts.why: An allowlist of configuration keys and their checks; a step of publishing that writes nothing of its own.

parts.name: Bundling through esbuild
parts.why: An adapter to esbuild.

parts.name: Python build
parts.why: A variant of bundling for a .py main that produces the same module records.

parts.name: Asset and image packaging
parts.why: Writes into the same deployment version and blob store as the other steps.

parts.name: Bucket publication
parts.why: Moves the pointers over the records the other steps prepared; one record set, so no part keeps state the others do not change.

components.name: Node
components.description: One celld process per machine: it serves the deployed Worker and its Durable Objects, owns the cells it runs, replicates their writes, and works with the other nodes of the fleet through the bucket and the peer protocol.

parts.name: Lifecycle executor (the Actor)
parts.why: The only caller of the decision core: it feeds it events and performs the effects it returns, so it passes requests on.

parts.name: Ownership, lease and drain adapters
parts.why: Serialization and bucket I/O for decisions the decision core makes; adapters through which it keeps its records.

parts.name: Request ingress and internal operator API
parts.why: Admit requests, ask the decision core for a route and forward them; they pass requests on.

parts.name: Peer transport
parts.why: The signed channel between nodes and its fleet secret, which is a credential rather than a resource.

parts.name: Fleet storage helpers
parts.why: fleet.rs opens bucket clients, runs the storage test and loads deployments for the other parts; it keeps nothing.

parts.name: Engine-neutral types
parts.why: engine_api.rs holds the types and helpers the cell runtime and the host share; part of the cell host contract.

parts.name: Dead-node clean-up
parts.why: Compatibility garbage collection of historical bucket debris; listed as a cleanup candidate.

components.name: Decision core
components.description: The node's pure decision-maker: from each event it decides which node owns a cell, when a cell starts, restores, moves or stops, where a request goes, when a response may leave, and how the node keeps, renews or loses its lease.

parts.name: Lifecycle state machine
parts.why: One State behind one on_event; no piece keeps state apart from it.

parts.name: Decision helpers
parts.why: Pure functions for the isolate pool, KV, queues, cron and the fleet log that keep no state, so they are libraries of the parts that call them.

components.name: Cell runtime
components.description: Runs the application in V8 isolates: Workers, Durable Objects with their SQLite storage, alarms and WebSockets, and the runtime-supplied cells behind KV, Queues, D1, Workflows and Cron Triggers.

parts.name: R2 binding
parts.why: An adapter that serves an r2_buckets binding out of the fleet bucket, shared with celld r2.

parts.name: Dynamic Worker loader and facets
parts.why: They run inside the Workers host's isolates and keep their state in its maps and in the root object's database.

components.name: Workers host
components.description: Runs Workers and ordinary Durable Objects in V8 isolates: it loads each deployment, keeps every Durable Object's SQLite database and WebSockets, and gives the application's code its bindings.

components.name: KV namespace service
components.description: The runtime-supplied cell behind a KV namespace: it stores the namespace's keys, values, metadata and expirations, with values above 1 MiB in the bucket.

components.name: Queue broker
components.description: The runtime-supplied cell behind a queue: it stores the messages sent to it, leases batches to the consumer script, applies acknowledgements, retries and dead-letter moves, and answers the operator's queue commands.

components.name: D1 database service
components.description: The runtime-supplied cell behind a D1 database: it runs the database's statements, batches and migrations in its own SQLite file.

components.name: Workflow engine
components.description: The runtime-supplied cell behind each Workflow instance: it replays run(), keeps finished step results, sleeps, waits for events and retries, and changes the instance's status on request.

components.name: Cron scheduler
components.description: The reserved cell that holds one script's cron schedule: it arms the next occurrence and calls the script's scheduled handler once per occurrence across the fleet, with retries.

components.name: Replication
components.description: Captures every committed write of every cell, proves it durable on follower nodes or in the bucket before the node answers, keeps each cell's history under its epoch prefix, and restores a cell from that history when a node takes it over.

parts.name: Cell replication backend
parts.why: Writes cells/<cell>/ltx/ and drains node bundles; it shares those records with the fleet log.

parts.name: Fleet log
parts.why: Its recovery writes the same per-cell LTX objects the backend writes, so the two change each other's records.

parts.name: LTX library
parts.why: A library (crates/ltx) used inside the durability protocol; it keeps nothing of its own.

components.name: Alarm discovery
components.description: Keeps a durable index of armed alarms in the bucket, so that an alarm fires even when its cell is out of memory or its node has stopped, and lets one node at a time scan it for alarms nobody else will fire.

parts.name: Publications and reclamation
parts.why: wake.rs writes the wake/ namespace that the arm gate and the format migration also write.

parts.name: Arm gate
parts.why: wake_entry.rs holds a response until its entry lands, over the same records.

parts.name: Format initialization and migration
parts.why: wake_format.rs initializes and migrates the same namespace.

components.name: Static asset server
components.description: Serves the deployment's static files, applying the _redirects and _headers rules and the html_handling and not_found_handling settings, and caches the files a node serves on its disk.

parts.name: Routing, disk cache and fallback index
parts.why: All inside one AssetResolver per script.

components.name: Container supervisor
components.description: Starts, watches and stops the one container a Durable Object can own, on the node that owns the object and behind a network fence, and enforces the fleet-wide instance cap.

parts.name: Docker Engine client
parts.why: docker.rs is an adapter to the container engine.

parts.name: Container ops
parts.why: js/container.rs only converts values for the supervisor.

components.name: Telemetry exporter
components.description: Records spans and log lines for the requests a node serves, and writes them as Parquet files to the bucket or sends them to an OpenTelemetry collector.

parts.name: OTLP encoding
parts.why: otlp.rs is a library that encodes the exporter's batches.

components.name: Managed agent
components.description: Connects a node to the hosted Managed Control Plane: it enrolls the installation, keeps its token and storage credentials, keeps a presence session that answers the control plane's questions about cells, and publishes the deployments made there.

parts.name: Enrollment and installation record
parts.why: The other pieces read and change the same record.

parts.name: Credential rotation
parts.why: Changes the same installation record.

parts.name: Operator commands
parts.why: celld token, credentials refresh and disconnect read or retire the same record.

parts.name: Presence session and explorer
parts.why: Read the decision core's presence projection and cell snapshots through the replication handle; they keep only the session.

parts.name: Deploy agent
parts.why: Writes deployment records through the node's deployment contract and keeps nothing of its own.

outsideServices.name: Object store
outsideServices.description: The operator's bucket on an S3-compatible store, Google Cloud Storage or Azure Blob Storage (a local SQLite store under celld dev), with the conditional writes, exact ranged reads and read-after-write consistency celld requires.

outsideServices.name: Container engine
outsideServices.description: A Docker or Podman daemon on the machine, reached through its command line when deploying and through its Engine API on a unix socket on a node.

outsideServices.name: Managed Control Plane
outsideServices.description: Deno's hosted service, at https://celld.dev by default, that enrolls celld installations, issues their storage credentials, accepts deployments from its console or from Wrangler, and shows their nodes and cells.

outsideServices.name: OpenTelemetry collector
outsideServices.description: A collector the operator names in CELLD_OTEL that receives traces and logs over OTLP/HTTP.

outsideServices.name: esbuild
outsideServices.description: The JavaScript bundler on the deploying machine's PATH, which builds a Worker's modules into one bundle.

outsideServices.name: Pyodide CDN
outsideServices.description: The jsDelivr host from which celld deploy downloads the pinned Pyodide 0.28.3 runtime the first time it builds a Python Worker.

resources.name: Deployment
resources.description: One version of the application: its Worker modules, configuration, bindings, Durable Object classes, cron schedule, static assets and container images, and the pointer that makes it current.

resources.name: Durable Object
resources.description: A named object of an application class with its own SQLite storage, one alarm and its WebSockets, which exactly one node runs at a time.

resources.name: Facet
resources.description: A child object inside a Durable Object, started from a class a Worker Loader provides, with a SQLite database of its own.

resources.name: Container
resources.description: The one container a Durable Object can start, reach over TCP and stop, running on the node that owns the object.

resources.name: Dynamic Worker
resources.description: Worker code that a running Worker loads at runtime through a Worker Loader binding, into an isolate of its own.

resources.name: KV namespace
resources.description: A key-value store a Worker binds by id, holding keys with their values, metadata and expirations.

resources.name: D1 database
resources.description: A SQL database a Worker binds by id or name, held in its own SQLite file.

resources.name: R2 object
resources.description: An object of an R2 bucket binding, stored under r2/<bucket_name>/ in the fleet bucket with its HTTP and custom metadata.

resources.name: Queue
resources.description: A named message queue with one consumer script, a pause flag and an optional dead-letter queue.

resources.name: Queue message
resources.description: One message sent to a queue, delivered at least once to the consumer in a batch until it is acknowledged, retried out or moved to the dead-letter queue.

resources.name: Workflow instance
resources.description: One run of a Workflow class, made of named steps, sleeps and event waits, with a status the application can read and change.

resources.name: Cron Trigger
resources.description: A cron expression of the deployment whose occurrences run the script's scheduled handler.

resources.name: Node
resources.description: One celld process: its lease in the bucket, its listeners, its load and the cells it owns.

resources.name: Fleet
resources.description: The nodes that share one bucket, with the settings that apply to all of them, such as whether ownership balancing is paused.

resources.name: Trace
resources.description: The spans and log lines recorded for one request, kept as Parquet files under telemetry/ in the bucket or sent to a collector.

resources.name: Managed installation
resources.description: A node's enrollment with the Managed Control Plane: its installation id and token, its credential version and its storage.

resources.name: Cell
resources.description: What the fleet owns and runs as one unit: a Durable Object, KV namespace, queue, D1 database, Workflow instance or cron schedule, with its owner node, fencing epoch and residency.

resources.name: Node log
resources.description: The tail of a node's committed writes that it has not yet uploaded, held on its followers' disks and described by its log/<node>.json record.

resources.name: Cell history
resources.description: A cell's replicated SQLite history, in LTX segments and snapshots under cells/<cell>/ltx/e<epoch>/, from which a node restores it.

resources.name: Wake entry
resources.description: The bucket record that makes an armed alarm discoverable: its entry under wake/entries/ and its retirement under wake/retired/.

resources.name: Static asset
resources.description: A file of the deployment's asset directory, with the headers and redirect rules that apply to it.

resources.name: Bucket object
resources.description: An object in the operator's bucket, written, read, listed and deleted by key, with an etag or generation for conditional writes.

resources.name: Container image
resources.description: An image a deployment names, built or pulled when deploying, saved under deploy/images/, then loaded into each node's engine.

resources.name: Worker bundle
resources.description: The JavaScript esbuild builds from a Worker's entry module and its imports.

resources.name: Pyodide release
resources.description: The pinned Pyodide 0.28.3 runtime files that a Python Worker build embeds.

resources.name: Managed deployment
resources.description: A deployment made in the Managed Control Plane, waiting as a command with the URLs of its modules and assets.

interfaces.name: Workers runtime API
interfaces.description: The JavaScript and Python API the application's code runs against: Workers handlers and env bindings for Durable Objects, KV, D1, R2, Queues, Workflows, Worker Loaders, assets and containers, as Cloudflare documents them.

interfaces.name: public Worker listener
interfaces.description: The node's public HTTP listener (--listen), which serves the deployed Worker and its static assets to the application's users.

interfaces.name: celld command line
interfaces.description: The celld binary: celld deploy, d1, kv, r2, queue, cell, diagnose and the managed-mode commands, and the node itself with its flags, environment variables and signals.

interfaces.name: local development server
interfaces.description: celld dev: one local node over a local store at .celld/dev, rebuilt when the project changes, on http://127.0.0.1:9876 by default.

interfaces.name: managed deployment
interfaces.description: A deployment made in the Managed Control Plane, from its console or with npx wrangler deploy and the exports celld token prints, which a managed node fetches and publishes.

interfaces.name: internal operator API
interfaces.description: The unauthenticated operator routes of the internal listener (--internal-listen): /state, /reload, /rebalance/pause and /resume, /shutdown, /cell/<scope>, /evict/<scope> and /do/<id>.

interfaces.name: node leases
interfaces.description: Each node's lease record nodes/<node>.json in the bucket, whose load block an autoscaler reads.

interfaces.name: deployment objects
interfaces.description: The deployment records of crates/celld/protocol.rs in the bucket: manifest, modules, asset index, image tars, queue consumer attachments, and the script and fleet pointers.

interfaces.name: presence hooks
interfaces.description: What a node hands the Managed agent at startup: a read-only presence snapshot from the decision core, the replication handle for cell snapshots, and the pointer watcher's nudge.

interfaces.name: managed installation API
interfaces.description: The Managed agent's functions the node calls at startup: enroll or confirm enrollment, read the installation's storage and credential version, wait for the first deployment, and report storage state.

interfaces.name: peer protocol
interfaces.description: The signed HTTP routes nodes use with each other on the internal listener: the /peer/tunnel stream for cell calls, /peer/log/* for the fleet log, /peer/handoff, /peer/abort and /peer/probe.

interfaces.name: object storage API
interfaces.description: The bucket's HTTP API as celld uses it: put, conditional create and overwrite, ranged get, list and delete, in the S3, Azure or Cloud Storage dialect.

interfaces.name: Docker Engine API
interfaces.description: The container engine's HTTP API on its unix socket, which a node uses to load images and run containers.

interfaces.name: docker command line
interfaces.description: The docker or Podman command on the deploying machine, which celld deploy runs to build, pull and save images.

interfaces.name: OTLP/HTTP
interfaces.description: The OpenTelemetry protocol over HTTP with protobuf bodies, sent to the collector's /v1/traces and /v1/logs.

interfaces.name: esbuild command line
interfaces.description: The esbuild executable, which celld deploy runs as a child process.

interfaces.name: Pyodide download
interfaces.description: HTTPS downloads of the Pyodide release files from cdn.jsdelivr.net, checked by size and SHA-256.

interfaces.name: Managed Control Plane agent API
interfaces.description: The control plane's HTTPS and WebSocket API under /api/instances and /api/agent, authenticated with the installation token.

interfaces.name: cell host contract
interfaces.description: The Actor's one boundary to the engine that runs cells (CellHost in crates/celld/cell_host.rs): start, dispatch, restore, prove durable, fire alarms, swap and stop.

interfaces.name: Actor mailbox
interfaces.description: The serial executor's queue of events into the decision core (Message in crates/celld/actor.rs), fed by the host channels of crates/celld/host_channels.rs and by the waker.

interfaces.name: replication handle
interfaces.description: The Replication wrapper of crates/celld/ltx_replication.rs, and the backend it hands out through ltx().

interfaces.name: node log manager
interfaces.description: The fleet log's manager (NodeLogManager in crates/celld/node_log.rs), which the Actor holds.

interfaces.name: ownership records
interfaces.description: The public functions of crates/celld/ownership_store.rs through which other parts read the decision core's ownership records, node leases and fleet sample, or hand it fields to publish in the node's lease.

interfaces.name: wake entry gate
interfaces.description: The functions of crates/celld/wake_entry.rs, with the WakeFlusher of crates/celld/wake.rs, that publish and maintain an alarm's wake entry and hold a response until it lands.

interfaces.name: asset resolver
interfaces.description: AssetResolver in crates/celld/assets.rs, one per script of the current deployment.

interfaces.name: container functions
interfaces.description: The supervisor's functions in crates/celld/container.rs that a Durable Object's container ops call.

interfaces.name: telemetry API
interfaces.description: start_trace, record and record_log in crates/celld/telemetry.rs.

interfaces.name: KV namespace cell protocol
interfaces.description: The methods of the KV namespace cell in crates/celld/js/services/kv.js that a KV binding calls through the namespace's stub.

interfaces.name: queue cell protocol
interfaces.description: The methods of the queue cell in crates/celld/js/harness.js that a producer binding calls, and the batches the cell leases to the consumer script.

interfaces.name: D1 cell protocol
interfaces.description: The fetch modes of the D1 database cell in crates/celld/js/harness.js: prepared, batch, exec and migrate.

interfaces.name: workflow cell protocol
interfaces.description: The __wf methods of the Workflow instance cell in crates/celld/js/harness.js.

interfaces.name: cron cell protocol
interfaces.description: The reserved cron cell's fetch, which arms a script's schedule after a deployment loads, and its alarm.

areas.name: Run the application
areas.description: Deploy the project and have its Workers and Durable Objects serve requests as on Cloudflare, each object run by one node and each write durable before it is answered.

capabilities.name: Deploy the application
capabilities.takes: a Wrangler project: its wrangler.json or wrangler.jsonc, Worker code, static assets and container images
capabilities.gives: a deployment that every node adopts in place, without a restart

capabilities.name: Serve requests
capabilities.takes: HTTP and WebSocket requests from the application's users
capabilities.gives: the responses of the Worker or of the static assets

capabilities.name: Call a Durable Object
capabilities.takes: an object id or name from its namespace, and a fetch, an RPC call or a WebSocket upgrade
capabilities.gives: the object's answer from the one node that runs it

capabilities.name: Read and write object storage
capabilities.takes: keys and values or SQL statements, inside the object's code, alone or in a transaction
capabilities.gives: the stored values and rows, with each write durable before the object's next output

capabilities.name: Set an object alarm
capabilities.takes: a time
capabilities.gives: a call of the object's alarm handler at that time, even after the object has left memory or its node has stopped

capabilities.name: Accept hibernatable WebSockets
capabilities.takes: a WebSocket the object accepts with ctx.acceptWebSocket()
capabilities.gives: clients that stay connected while the object hibernates, and a handler call for each message

areas.name: Store data
areas.description: Keep the application's data in KV namespaces, D1 databases and R2 buckets, from Worker code or from the command line.

capabilities.name: Read and write KV keys
capabilities.takes: a namespace and keys with values, metadata and expirations, or a Wrangler bulk file
capabilities.gives: the stored values, their metadata and key listings, never stale

capabilities.name: Query a D1 database
capabilities.takes: a database and SQL statements, prepared, batched or as a script
capabilities.gives: rows, results and metadata, a batch run in one transaction

capabilities.name: Apply D1 migrations
capabilities.takes: a database and the project's migrations directory
capabilities.gives: the migrations not yet applied, applied in order

capabilities.name: Read and write R2 objects
capabilities.takes: a bucket binding and keys with bodies, metadata, ranges and conditions, or a multipart upload
capabilities.gives: the stored objects, their records and listings

areas.name: Run background work
areas.description: Send messages to queues and consume them, run Workflows, and run scheduled handlers.

capabilities.name: Send queue messages
capabilities.takes: a queue and one message or a batch of up to 100
capabilities.gives: the messages committed to the queue

capabilities.name: Consume queue messages
capabilities.takes: a consumer script with a queue handler, and its batching, retry and dead-letter settings
capabilities.gives: batches of messages delivered at least once, each acknowledged, retried or moved to the dead-letter queue

capabilities.name: Operate a queue
capabilities.takes: a queue and info, peek, purge, pause, resume or redrive
capabilities.gives: the queue's state, or the queue paused, resumed, purged or with its dead letters redriven

capabilities.name: Start a Workflow
capabilities.takes: a Workflow binding and the parameters of one instance or a batch
capabilities.gives: running instances whose steps, sleeps and event waits survive node failures

capabilities.name: Read a Workflow instance's status
capabilities.takes: an instance id
capabilities.gives: its status, output or error

capabilities.name: Change a Workflow instance's status
capabilities.takes: an instance and pause, resume, restart, terminate or delete
capabilities.gives: the instance with its new status

capabilities.name: Send an event to a Workflow instance
capabilities.takes: an instance, an event type and a payload
capabilities.gives: the event delivered to the instance's matching wait, or held until it reaches one

capabilities.name: Run Cron Triggers
capabilities.takes: the deployment's triggers.crons expressions and a scheduled handler
capabilities.gives: one call of the handler for each occurrence across the fleet, retried on failure

areas.name: Load code at runtime
areas.description: Run code that the application supplies while it runs, and give that code durable storage.

capabilities.name: Load a Dynamic Worker
capabilities.takes: Worker code through a Worker Loader binding: modules, compatibility date, env, egress policy, limits and tail Workers
capabilities.gives: a Fetcher or RPC stub for the loaded Worker, which runs in its own isolate

capabilities.name: Start a facet
capabilities.takes: a name and a class from a Worker Loader or ctx.exports, inside a Durable Object
capabilities.gives: a stub for a child object with its own SQLite database, which can be aborted or deleted by name

areas.name: Run containers
areas.description: Run a program that is not JavaScript beside a Durable Object.

capabilities.name: Run a container
capabilities.takes: a Durable Object of a containers class, and start options, ports, signals or processes to run
capabilities.gives: a container on the object's node, reachable over TCP, signalled or stopped on request

areas.name: Run the fleet
areas.description: Start, add, stop and upgrade nodes against one bucket, and see how they and the fleet are doing.

capabilities.name: Start a node
capabilities.takes: the fleet bucket and its credentials, the listener and advertised addresses, and tuning variables
capabilities.gives: a node that passes the bucket's storage test, joins the fleet through its lease and serves the current deployment

capabilities.name: Stop a node
capabilities.takes: SIGTERM or SIGINT, or POST /shutdown, optionally with handoff=preserve
capabilities.gives: a node that stops taking requests, hands its cells to peers with their data proven durable, and exits

capabilities.name: Read node state
capabilities.takes: a node
capabilities.gives: its live counters and load: owned and resident cells, waiting activations, memory, pressure, isolates and deployments

capabilities.name: Diagnose the fleet
capabilities.takes: the fleet bucket, and optionally some node ids
capabilities.gives: for each node lease whether it is live, its address valid and the peer reachable and compatible, with its load; and whether the bucket passes the conditional-write test

capabilities.name: Reload the deployment
capabilities.takes: POST /reload on a node
capabilities.gives: the node serving the current deployment now, or the build error

capabilities.name: Pause or resume balancing
capabilities.takes: POST /rebalance/pause or /rebalance/resume on any node
capabilities.gives: ownership balancing paused or resumed for the whole fleet

areas.name: Manage cells
areas.description: Find, inspect and act on the Durable Objects the fleet holds.

capabilities.name: List Durable Objects
capabilities.takes: the fleet bucket, and optionally a class, a page size or a continuation
capabilities.gives: one Class:ID scope per instance, with reserved classes marked

capabilities.name: Preview epoch cleanup
capabilities.takes: the fleet bucket and a grace period
capabilities.gives: for each cell, the epoch prefixes epoch GC could delete, their bytes and the restore base, with nothing written

capabilities.name: Locate a cell
capabilities.takes: a cell scope
capabilities.gives: the node that owns the cell, which is activated if needed

capabilities.name: Evict a cell
capabilities.takes: a cell scope
capabilities.gives: the cell out of memory with its data durable, or the reason the node refused

capabilities.name: Call a Durable Object directly
capabilities.takes: an ordinary Durable Object id and a request
capabilities.gives: the object's response

areas.name: Observe requests
areas.description: Record traces and logs of the requests the fleet serves.

questions.question: Is the Managed Control Plane a consumer of celld or a service celld uses?
questions.answer: An outside service of the Managed agent, rather than a second Level 1 consumer. The node holds the control URL and a bearer installation token, opens every connection, and calls the control plane's API for enrollment, credentials, deploy tokens and deployment commands, which is how the extraction rules recognize an outside service. But the control plane also asks the node for presence and cell tables over the session the node opened, and a person uses its console to deploy and browse, so it could be read as a consumer with goals of its own. The checker refuses one name as both, and no rule says which direction should carry everything.

questions.question: Are the application developer and the fleet operator one role or two?
questions.answer: Two consumers rather than one self-hosting team. Their goals diverge (code and data on one side, nodes, bucket and rollouts on the other), and the documentation addresses them in separate sections, but in a small team one person holds both roles.

questions.question: Whose boundary holds celld d1, kv, r2 and queue?
questions.answer: The developer's, as a second interface of the binding capabilities (Query a D1 database, Read and write KV keys, Read and write R2 objects) plus Apply D1 migrations and Operate a queue, rather than the operator's, where README.md lists them under Operate a fleet. They work on the application's data and replace wrangler d1, kv and r2 commands, but the README frames them as fleet operations.

questions.question: Is operating the fleet a product use or engineering tooling?
questions.answer: A product use: starting and stopping nodes, diagnose, cell list, epoch-cleanup preview, eviction and balancing are the operator's capabilities, because celld is self-hosted infrastructure and these are documented for its users. The rule that leaves out tools that set a system up, deploy it or diagnose it could have excluded the whole operator boundary.

questions.question: Should Level 2 be the node and the tools, or the node's insides?
questions.answer: Deployment publisher, Node and Managed agent at Level 2, with the decision core, cell runtime and replication inside the Node at Level 3, rather than those parts directly at Level 2. protocol.rs declares the deployment records as the interface between deployment tools and nodes, and the node is reached only through its listeners and records; the alternative removes one level and with it the Node <-> Node peer boundary.

questions.question: Are the Deployment publisher and the Managed agent one component, since both write the deployment records and pointers?
questions.answer: Two consumers of the node's deployment contract rather than one component. The shared-store rule points to one component, but protocol.rs calls those records the interface between deployment tools and celld, and each tool writes them with its own code (deploy.rs put_pointer, control_plane.rs apply_deployment).

questions.question: Do the decision core and Replication share one record?
questions.answer: Yes: the fleet log's root record moved into the node lease (NodeLogWire in ownership_store.rs: the record moved into the lease). The fleet log hands its record to the lease writer through set_own_log, and on recovery CASes a stopped node's lease itself (node_log.rs write_dead_record). The map keeps two components, with a Replication <-> Decision core boundary on ownership records, rather than one, because the celld-logic crate boundary is stronger evidence than the shared record; the direct CAS of a stopped node's lease is the one write that goes outside the decision core's adapter.

questions.question: Where do the decision helpers of crates/logic belong?
questions.answer: With the Decision core rather than with the components that call them (isolate.rs with the isolate pool, kv.rs with the KV namespace service, queue.rs with the Queue broker, cron.rs with the Cron scheduler, log_tier.rs and epoch_gc.rs with Replication). The crate's no-dependency rule makes it one part, and the helpers keep no state, so they create no boundary; a reader tracing a KV or queue rule should look in crates/logic.

questions.question: Is the Actor a component?
questions.answer: A part of the Node that passes events to the decision core and performs its effects, rather than a Lifecycle executor component; its files and the ownership, lease and drain adapters are placed with the Decision core so a change to them traces to the boundaries they carry out.

questions.question: Is the fleet log a component of its own?
questions.answer: Inside Replication rather than beside it. It has its own peer routes and records, but its recovery writes the per-cell LTX objects the replication backend writes, and the backend drains the bundles the fleet log keeps.

questions.question: Are KV, Queues, D1, Workflows and Cron components or features of the Workers host?
questions.answer: Level 4 components inside the Cell runtime rather than parts of the Workers host. Each is a runtime-supplied Durable Object class registered by __runtimeClass (or .cron), whose cell alone changes its rows and is reached only through its cell protocol, though all of them run on the Workers host like any Durable Object.

questions.question: Where does crates/celld/js/harness.js sit?
questions.answer: With the Workers host, rather than split, because a place names whole files: the file also holds the Queue broker, D1 database service, Workflow engine and Cron scheduler cell classes, so a change to it can touch any of those five components.

questions.question: Are the Static asset server, Container supervisor and Telemetry exporter components or parts of the cell runtime?
questions.answer: Components of the Node, because each keeps state or makes decisions alone and is reached through one API (AssetResolver, the container functions, the telemetry API), rather than parts of the Cell runtime, whose generation holds the asset resolvers and whose ops call the other two.

questions.question: Do the calls into ownership_store.rs from other components go around the decision core's contract?
questions.answer: They go through its public functions, so the map treats them as the ownership records interface rather than as bypasses: the waker reads owner records before waking a cell, the container supervisor reads the fleet's container counts from the capacity sample before a start, and the Workers host reads the shedding flag before a stateless dispatch. These are checks folded into the capabilities they decide, so only the fleet log's lease reads and record hand-over have capabilities of their own.

questions.question: Does the Workers host reach past the replication handle?
questions.answer: It uses the backend that Replication::ltx() hands out (activation_vfs, discard, is_resident, delete_local, delete_streams in runtime.rs and facet_streams.rs), although ltx_replication.rs says nothing else touches the backend. The map counts ltx() as part of the replication handle's contract rather than as a bypass, since the handle exposes it on purpose.

questions.question: Do the cell listings in celld cell and the Managed agent's explorer bypass the node?
questions.answer: They list the cells/ prefix of the bucket directly, and celld cell gc --dry-run reads epochs through the replication backend, rather than asking a node. The map accepts these as read-only listings of the cell inventory by interface pieces rather than listing them as cleanup.

questions.question: Do the Deployment publisher and the Managed agent reach into the Static asset server and the Container supervisor?
questions.answer: They call pure validation helpers there (validate_asset_file_size and is_canonical_asset_path in assets.rs; image_key, image_reference and instance_resources in container.rs) so that "the builder, managed agent, and serving node" apply one size and naming policy. The map treats these as shared library functions rather than boundaries, because they keep no state; moving them to a shared policy module would make that explicit.

questions.question: Which resource does Serve requests work on?
questions.answer: It observes the Deployment, whose code and assets answer, rather than producing a resource: a response is an output, not something the developer manages.

questions.question: Is a deployment made in the Managed Control Plane an interface of celld?
questions.answer: An interface of the developer's Deploy the application, rather than left out as the control plane's own channel, because celld token prints the Wrangler exports for it and a managed node fetches and publishes what arrives.

questions.question: Is the health path a capability?
questions.answer: Excluded as load-balancer machinery, rather than an operator capability, although the readiness it reports paces rolling upgrades.

cleanupCandidates.name: Dead-node compatibility clean-up (crates/celld/dead_node_gc.rs)
cleanupCandidates.why: Compatibility garbage collection that retires historical node-cells/ index debris and expired node-session records left in fleet buckets; serving correctness no longer depends on it.

cleanupCandidates.name: v0.4.1 wake-index migration (crates/celld/wake_format.rs, crates/celld/storage/wake_record.rs)
cleanupCandidates.why: Upgrades a stopped v0.4.1 fleet's alarm discovery (the old wake-format.json, wake-v2/ and wake-retired-v2/ names, discovery seeds) and installs identities for legacy alarms; needed only for fleets coming from v0.4.1.

cleanupCandidates.name: LTX legacy frame layout (crates/ltx/src/codec.rs)
cleanupCandidates.why: The ordinary L0 writer still emits the v0.5.1 frame representation and the reader keeps a dual decoder, so a mixed fleet must set CELLD_LTX_COMPACTION=0 until every node reads block files (crates/ltx/README.md).

cleanupCandidates.name: CLT1 node-log tails (crates/celld/node_log.rs)
cleanupCandidates.why: An older node's entries-only tail format still accepted during recovery; docs/guarantees.md says it proves neither completeness nor loss and can stall a mixed-version update.

cleanupCandidates.name: Removed-settings guard (crates/celld/env_vars.rs)
cleanupCandidates.why: The REMOVED table refuses retired variables such as CELLD_OUTPUT_GATE, CELLD_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS, CELLD_AI_BINDING and CELLD_OTEL_SINK at startup, so old configurations fail loudly.

cleanupCandidates.name: AI metadata guard for old managed uploads (crates/celld/fleet.rs)
cleanupCandidates.why: Refuses a deployment that still carries an ai binding from before the AI adapter was removed, because "Old managed uploads can contain AI metadata without a required-feature gate".

cleanupCandidates.name: Old-path re-exports and the absent workerd arm (crates/celld/engine_api.rs, host_channels.rs, http_streams.rs, ws_registry.rs, wake_entry.rs, kv_blob.rs, queue_policy.rs, js/services/kv.js)
cleanupCandidates.why: Items are re-exported "at its old path" from crate::js, and several seams are written for a workerd engine arm that is not in the repository.

cleanupCandidates.name: Temporary host seam (crates/celld/lib.rs)
cleanupCandidates.why: worker_compat is introduced as a "Temporary host seam required by the verbatim JS adapter".

cleanupCandidates.name: Single-database scope column (crates/celld/storage.rs)
cleanupCandidates.why: The scope column "survives from the single-db era and still keys rows", although each database now holds one cell.

cleanupCandidates.name: Installation record aliases (crates/celld/control_plane.rs)
cleanupCandidates.why: CloudConfig accepts the older instance_id and instance_token field names, and NodeLogWire keeps the JSON key active for compatibility.

excluded.name: Users of the deployed application
excluded.why: HTTP and WebSocket clients of the developer's Worker use the developer's application, which celld serves through the developer's boundary.

excluded.name: Health path /.well-known/celld/health
excluded.why: A boolean for load balancers and orchestrators: machinery nobody uses for a purpose of their own.

excluded.name: Fleet placement and memory behavior
excluded.why: Ownership balancing, memory-pressure shedding, idle eviction and hibernation, the residency cap and handing a cold activation to the least-loaded peer are what celld does on its own.

excluded.name: Ownership safety machinery
excluded.why: Node lease renewal and self-fencing, the takeover recovery gate, the output gate's waiting and the storage test at startup are provider behavior behind the developer's and operator's capabilities.

excluded.name: Storage housekeeping
excluded.why: Epoch GC, L1 compaction, the paged background fill, wake-entry clean-up and the waker's orphan scan, telemetry retention and local cache pruning run on their own.

excluded.name: Rollout pacing
excluded.why: The fleet drain token, the first-readiness gate and deployment pointer polling pace rollouts without anyone calling them.

excluded.name: Limits and overload refusals
excluded.why: Per-cell admission (CELLD_MAX_CELL_REQUESTS), body limits, KV, D1, Queue, R2 and Dynamic Worker limits are constraints of the capabilities, not capabilities.

excluded.name: Runtime APIs without a celld resource
excluded.why: fetch, streams, Web Crypto, Node.js compatibility, HTMLRewriter, TCP sockets, EventSource, MessageChannel, timers and the always-miss Cache are the Worker's language environment and keep no state celld holds.

excluded.name: Unsupported Cloudflare services
excluded.why: Workers AI, Vectorize, Hyperdrive, Browser Rendering, Email Workers, BroadcastChannel and the tail and email handlers are documented as not implemented and have no code.

excluded.name: Peer probe
excluded.why: /peer/probe is a signed diagnostic that celld diagnose sends to check a lease's node; a step of diagnosing.

excluded.name: Build, check and release tooling
excluded.why: The release workflow, the Dockerfile, the Cargo manifests and the clippy architecture lints work on celld itself; clippy.toml was read as evidence of the execution boundary.

excluded.name: Test suites and the simulated execution backend
excluded.why: crates/celld/lib.rs includes them from outside the tree with include!(env!(...)); they are not in the repository.

excluded.name: Installer
excluded.why: celld.dev/install.sh, which the documentation names, is not in the repository.
